notes: The project's one pre-declared primary comparison for Analyze, run live through the engine's /stats/hypothesis/run: are early-morning (07:00-08:30) and late-morning (08:30-10:00) wait times different? Raw values are the baseline dataset's wait_minutes split by its daypart stratification column (60 early / 60 late, the split the collection plan captured for exactly this use). Declared before looking at the data; comparisons_declared=1, tests run=1. Interpretation is in analyze/hypothesis-note.md -- effect size and CI quoted against the 3.4-minute gap, per R-ANA-05.

value.effect_size_ci_method: Hedges & Olkin (1985) large-sample approximate SE -- not an exact noncentral-t CI
assumptions_checked: n >= 8 per sample cleared (matrix §4a EXIT-06); groups independent

plain_language.comparison_summary: Compared early (07:00-08:30) (n=60, mean=8.182) against late (08:30-10:00) (n=60, mean=8.635) using Welch's two-sample t-test (unequal variances assumed by default -- no equal-variance check to trip on).
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.0165, below the alpha=0.05 threshold: if there were truly no difference, a result at least this far from 'no difference' would turn up by chance alone only about 1.7% of the time. That makes the difference statistically detectable here -- it does not mean the null hypothesis is false with that probability, and it says nothing yet about whether the difference is big enough to matter.
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Cohen's d = -0.44 -- a small difference (Cohen 1988 conventional bands: negligible<0.2, small<0.5, medium<0.8, large>=0.8).
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.

provenance.method: Welch's two-sample t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind, equal_var=False; NIST/SEMATECH §7.3.1 unequal-variance form + Welch-Satterthwaite df) + Cohen's d on the unweighted-average SD (Delacre, Lakens & Leys 2017)
